summary: The shell layer is ~4,060 lines across 13 scripts. `longrun.sh` (1,968 lines, 161 kB — most of it commentary/lab notebook) is the live entry point: it dispatches 12 subcommands (`fetch`, `run|resume`, `pilot`, `pilot-add`, `add`, `grid`, `seeds`, `repeat`, `smoke`, `ladder`, `pair`, `watch`) and holds a single `_flags_for()` table of 99 named arms plus 21 curated presets (`pilots`/`ablate`/`tokens`/`fabric`/`round3`..`round18`). Its own invariants are an append-only `runs/` tree (`_reserve`), a config fingerprint written beside every finished log (`_cfgsig`/`_reusable`), a completion marker (`_done`) that drives resume-skip, and a corpus bootstrapper (`_pilot_corpus`). `preflight.sh` gates a fresh (aarch64/GH200) box, `selftest.sh` is the project test entry point (16 unit suites + a CPU train + a CPU resume; it passes at HEAD), and `harness_test.sh` is the only test of the shell itself. `equiv.sh` answers "did this commit change behaviour" by running two git worktrees and diffing normalised logs. The remaining scripts are older strata: `rerun.sh`, `run_full_unfrozen.sh`, `run_cl_test.sh`, `bench_gpu.sh`, `sweep_domains.sh`, `sweep_domain_grid.sh`, `fetch_data.sh`, `fetch_40g.sh` — none is exercised by `selftest.sh`, several grep for report lines that no longer exist, one (`sweep_domain_grid.sh`) cannot start at all, and one (`run_full_unfrozen.sh`) is still the README's headline command while hardcoding pre-2026-08-17 fabric geometry. The dominant live bug class here is exactly the project's own: arms that are armed but inert — six arm names resolve to a flag set identical to the shipped defaults, and three of those sit in the same curated list as `base`.

levers.name: OUT
levers.effect: root for pilot/pilot-add/run/resume/add artefacts; also the whole output dir for rerun.sh (defaults to runs/rerun_<date>).

levers.name: DATA_DIR
levers.effect: corpus root for fetch/run/resume/add (the GB-scale half of the harness). Never consulted by pilot/grid/seeds/repeat.

levers.name: PILOT_DIR
levers.effect: corpus root for pilot/pilot-add/grid/seeds/repeat/smoke, and the ONLY directory `_corpsig` fingerprints.

levers.name: PILOT_GB
levers.effect: size `_pilot_corpus` pulls when train/eng has no part*.txt, and the default fourth argument of `pilot-add`.

levers.name: STREAM_LEN
levers.effect: bytes per epoch. Independent of PILOT_GB, so a 0.06 GB corpus will happily serve a 94 MB/epoch stream with only a runtime warning.
levers.owner: self_organize.py; set on every harness env line
levers.evidence: longrun.sh:543, :617, :1121; the coupling is documented at longrun.sh:1362-1370

levers.name: EPOCHS
levers.effect: passes over the stream. An arm may override it (vmax8k sets EPOCHS=18) and the grid banner still prints the harness value.

levers.name: DEVICE
levers.effect: cuda/cpu for every subcommand except `run|resume`, which hardcodes DEVICE=cuda. selftest.sh deliberately ignores it.

levers.name: SIG_WIN
levers.effect: signature window; pinned to 614 on every long/pilot/grid env line so the encoder covers the mature loop stride.

levers.name: GRID_DIR
levers.effect: output directory for `grid`. Separating rounds by directory is the only thing that stops round11/round12 (identical arm lists) colliding.

levers.name: GRID_ARMS
levers.effect: overrides the arm list — including an explicitly-passed preset name, silently.

levers.name: GRID_CKPT
levers.effect: 1 (default) reserves a checkpoint dir per arm; anything else passes SAVE_CKPT=0, which also moves the tokenizer save target to TOKENIZER_PATH.

levers.name: SEED_CKPT
levers.effect: 1 (default) writes a checkpoint per seed — changed from 0 because continual learning needs something to resume from.
levers.evidence: longrun.sh:1671 and the note at longrun.sh:1626-1630

levers.name: SEEDS
levers.effect: explicit seed list, overriding the count argument. Exported by `pair` and `ladder` so the child `seeds` invocations are paired by construction.

levers.name: SEED
levers.effect: read by `repeat` as the fixed seed to repeat; not read by `seeds` (which varies it).

levers.name: STOP_FILE
levers.effect: overrides the default `<dir>/STOP` cooperative-stop path for grid/seeds/repeat/ladder.

levers.name: SMOKE_ARMS
levers.effect: arm list for `smoke`. Default is 7 tokenizer-focused arms; the banner calls it "every pilot arm".

levers.name: RESUME_FROM
levers.effect: points `pilot-add` at any checkpoint directory instead of $OUT/pilot_<arch>. Consumed by the shell and stripped with `env -u` so the config audit does not flag it.

levers.name: PURE_ADD
levers.effect: 1 sets PHASE_SCHED so ONLY the added area is streamed — the arm the catastrophic-forgetting claim rests on. pilot-add only.

levers.name: FETCH_ARGS
levers.effect: passthrough to fetch_big.py / fetch_local.py (--data-dir, --token, --allow-short). An explicit --data-dir suppresses the automatic the-stack language directory.

levers.name: PILOT_ARCH / PILOT_ADD_ARCH / TF_LAYERS
levers.effect: base LM for pilot and pilot-add. Defaults to gru only; the transformer arm is documented as answered and switched off.

levers.name: LADDER_BASE
levers.effect: reuse a completed baseline rung from another ladder instead of re-running it; compare.py checks commit and corpus but nothing else.

levers.name: SELFTEST_DIR / SELFTEST_DEVICE / SELFTEST_DATA
levers.effect: artefact dir, training device (cpu unless set), and corpus dir for selftest.sh's end-to-end legs.

levers.name: SCALE / LEN / SEED
levers.effect: equiv.sh's configuration: fast (default, ~2-4 min/side) vs deep (~15-25 min/side), stream length override, and seed. None of the three appears in the output directory name or in any config stamp.

levers.name: SMOKE
levers.effect: preflight.sh section 9 on/off. SMOKE=0 skips the only check that actually runs the product path.

levers.name: FIX
levers.effect: NOTHING. Documented in preflight.sh's usage header as "also install what is missing"; the name appears nowhere else in the file.
levers.evidence: preflight.sh:12 is the only occurrence of FIX in the file

levers.name: STEPS / BPT / WIN / ONLY / SKIP_FETCH / DATA / GB / TRF_LAYERS
levers.effect: bench_gpu.sh matrix control. STEPS is a target, not a count: STREAM_LEN = STEPS*WIN*BPT and BPT is a hand-set 1.85 bytes/token estimate.

levers.name: SMOKE_JOBS / SMOKE_LEN
levers.effect: parallelism and stream length of rerun.sh's smoke gate. SMOKE_JOBS defaults to nproc; all parallel arms share one tokenizer output path.

levers.name: STAGES / JOBS / MAX_MIN / KEY_SRC / BIG / FORCE / DRY / SKIP_GPU_CHECK
levers.effect: sweep_domain_grid.sh control. FORCE=1 bypasses the unpinned-knob (4b) and inherited-knob (4c) guards but NOT the section-4 knob check, which currently kills the script unconditionally.

levers.name: GB / OUT / DATASET / DOMAIN / VENV / LOG
levers.effect: fetch_40g.sh pull parameters. GB is not persisted, so `status` always compares on-disk bytes against whatever GB is set in the status invocation.

levers.name: BIG
levers.effect: fetch_data.sh: 1 adds two large GitHub-hosted Gutenberg corpora on top of the ~45 MB NLTK set.

levers.name: RUN_NAME
levers.effect: run_full_unfrozen.sh: namespaces log (~/$RUN.txt), checkpoint (runs/$RUN) and tokenizer (data/tok_$RUN.json).

carry_forward.item: An arm's flag set must be diffed against _SPEC OVERLAID WITH the subcommand's own hardcoded env line — not against _SPEC alone. `vmax4k` (VMAX=4096) is inert against the registry but live inside `grid`, which hardcodes VMAX=2048; `frozen`'s SEED_VOCAB=512 is inert against the registry but live inside `smoke`, which hardcodes 256.
carry_forward.why: Either baseline used alone gives the wrong answer about which arms are real, in opposite directions.

carry_forward.item: Arm flags MUST be the last assignments on the env line. `env A=1 A=2` keeps the last, and every subcommand hardcodes VMAX/WIN/BATCH_W/CKPT_EVERY/GROW_*/SEG_*/DATA_DIR after which the arm's own value must come.
carry_forward.why: With flags first, `grid 3 VMAX=512` ran at 2048 and labelled the log 512. The invariant is stated four times in the file and is what makes arm-level overrides mean anything.

carry_forward.item: `_reserve` deliberately shares one counter between `<name>` and `<name>.log`; its while-loop tests BOTH forms. This is what keeps a run's checkpoint and its log on the same numeric suffix when one of the two is missing. Do not 'simplify' it to test only the path it was given.
carry_forward.why: Without the coupling, a crashed run that wrote a log but no checkpoint puts the next run's ckpt at -2 and its log at -3, filing a result under a name that does not match the model that produced it.

carry_forward.item: A run's vocabulary is saved to SAVE_CKPT+'.dyntok.json', never back to the TOKENIZER_PATH it read; and a RESUME with SAVE_CKPT=0 saves no vocabulary at all. Any harness that sets TOKENIZER_PATH without SAVE_CKPT is choosing the save target; any harness that sets both is choosing read and write independently.
carry_forward.why: The old coupling let a resume overwrite its parent's vocabulary, which made the parent checkpoint permanently unloadable (VOCABULARY MISMATCH). This is the single most load-bearing shell/engine contract.

carry_forward.item: On a resume with no TOKENIZER_PATH, self_organize.py defaults to `<RESUME>.dyntok.json`, and a FRESH online run never loads a vocabulary file at all (`os.path.exists(_tp) and (not TOK_ONLINE or RESUME)`). That is why `run|resume` can omit TOKENIZER_PATH safely and why equiv.sh's worktrees are deterministic despite a tracked data/ directory.
carry_forward.why: Removing either half of that condition silently re-enables the shared-data/dyntok.json pairing that pilot-add's fallback warns about.

carry_forward.item: Both `pilot-add` and `add` must read the checkpoint's fab_cfg and export FAB_N0, FAB_NMAX (2x cap), VMAX (2x V, NOT 2x tok_vocab), FAB_RANK and FAB_DK, each behind its OWN `[ -z "${X:-}" ]` test. Nesting them inside one gate meant that setting FAB_N0 by hand silently reverted VMAX to 2048 and FAB_NMAX to 4096.
carry_forward.why: rank and dk are INNER tensor dimensions and cannot be widened; cap and V are outer and must be doubled or the added area gets experts but no tokens, and the cull gate stays shut for the run.
carry_forward.evidence: longrun.sh:770-807 (pilot-add), longrun.sh:990-1010 (add); the V-vs-tok_vocab reasoning is inline at longrun.sh:752-757

carry_forward.item: `_cfgsig` derives its knob list from _SPEC by sed, so adding a knob to the registry automatically extends the run fingerprint. Do not replace it with a hand-picked list: the FAB_LR_CYCLE bisect lost two arms to one log because the log NAME derived from ARMFLAGS and an exported knob reached neither the name nor the signature.

carry_forward.item: `grid`, `seeds` and `repeat` stop cleanly via `touch <dir>/STOP` (or STOP_FILE=<path>): the run in flight finishes and writes its report and checkpoint, then the loop breaks. Ctrl-C kills the current run; killing the shell orphans the python.
carry_forward.why: There is no other way to end a multi-hour sweep without losing the arm in flight.
